audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7702 authorization nonce properly validated to prevent same-chain replay attacks?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: The nonce validation in verifyAuthorities at line 689-693 compares auth.Nonce against authorityNonce from state. The check `authorityNonce != auth.Nonce` ensures exact match. After successful authorization, nonce is incremented at line 719.
identified_risks: Nonce comparison is exact match, preventing replay of same-nonce authorizations
Nonce increment happens atomically after code delegation

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Conforms to EIP-7702 specification - nonce must match current account nonce exactly
edge_cases_analyzed: Nonce overflow: MaxUint64 check exists in RecoverSigner

audit_items.auditor_notes: EIP-7702 nonce validation correctly implemented. Nonce check at line 689 ensures exact match with current state nonce. Replay protection confirmed.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-020: Does encode_account receive a correct 32-byte storage_root Merkle root from all callers?

code_scope.reason: SPECIFICATION-ONLY - encode_account is a specification-level function not directly implemented in EL

audit_items.auditor_notes: This checklist item refers to encode_account which is a specification-level concept. The actual account encoding in Erigon is handled through state trie operations which have different interfaces.

audit_items.title: Can type alias constructors (Address, Root, VersionedHash, Bloom) be bypassed to create instances with incorrect byte lengths?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Address is [20]byte, Hash is [32]byte, Bloom is [256]byte - these are fixed-size arrays in Go. Type safety is enforced at compile time. BytesToAddress truncates/pads to exactly 20 bytes.
identified_risks: Go fixed-size arrays provide compile-time length enforcement
BytesToAddress and similar functions handle variable-length input safely

edge_cases_analyzed: Input longer than expected: Truncated (takes last N bytes for Address)

audit_items.auditor_notes: Go's type system with fixed-size arrays provides compile-time enforcement. Constructor functions handle edge cases appropriately.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-018: Does parse_deposit_requests enforce deterministic receipt key ordering across all execution clients?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: ParseDepositLogs iterates over logs slice in order. The logs are provided by block execution in transaction index order (deterministic). Each log is filtered by address and topic before processing.
identified_risks: Log ordering depends on execution layer providing logs in deterministic order
Filter checks: l.Address == depositContractAddress && len(l.Topics) > 0 && l.Topics[0] == depositTopic

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Conforms to EIP-6110 - deposits processed in receipt order

audit_items.auditor_notes: Deposit parsing follows deterministic log iteration order. Cross-client consistency relies on identical log ordering from block execution.

audit_items.title: Verify execution client consensus: Do all compliant execution clients produce identical requests_hash for the same block?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: requests_hash is computed from the concatenation of deposit request data in transaction order. The implementation follows EIP-6110 specification.
identified_risks: Cross-client consistency depends on all clients implementing EIP-6110 correctly

phase3_findings.formal_property: ∀ client1, client2: requests_hash(client1, block) == requests_hash(client2, block)
remaining_concerns: Cross-client testing required for full verification

audit_items.auditor_notes: Implementation appears correct but cross-client testing is required to verify identical output across all EL implementations.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does trie_get properly validate and handle missing receipt keys from untrusted P2P blocks?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: ParseDepositLogs receives logs that have already been validated through block execution. The function does not directly access receipt trie - logs are pre-extracted during block processing.
identified_risks: Receipt trie validation occurs during block import, before ParseDepositLogs is called
Invalid blocks are rejected at block validation layer

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Block validation layer handles receipt trie integrity

remaining_concerns: Block validation layer must be verified separately

audit_items.auditor_notes: Deposit parsing operates on pre-validated logs. Receipt trie integrity is enforced at block validation layer.

audit_items.title: Is the receipts trie integrity validated before parse_deposit_requests processes receipt keys?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Receipts are generated during block execution and their trie root is validated against the block header. ParseDepositLogs receives logs after this validation.

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Standard Ethereum block validation includes receipt root verification

audit_items.auditor_notes: Block validation ensures receipt trie integrity before deposit processing.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-022: Can an attacker forge a transaction signature that recovers to a different sender address?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: recoverPlain validates V bit length, checks signature validity via TransactionSignatureIsValid, then calls secp256k1.RecoverPubkey. The recovered address is derived from the public key hash.
identified_risks: Signature validation includes s-value range check (EIP-2)
V value restricted to 0 or 1
r and s must be non-zero and less than secp256k1N

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Conforms to Ethereum Yellow Paper Appendix F
edge_cases_analyzed: Malleable signatures: Rejected (s > secp256k1halfN check when homestead=true)

audit_items.auditor_notes: Transaction signature recovery is correctly implemented with proper ECDSA validation.

audit_items.title: Verify Execution Client Transaction Authentication: Does the execution client properly validate recovered sender addresses?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Sender is recovered from signature on each transaction validation. No caching of sender from external sources.

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Standard ECDSA recovery per Ethereum specification

audit_items.auditor_notes: Sender recovery performed independently using raw signature data.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006/tb-001: Is ECDSA signature verification correctly enforced for all EIP-7702 Authorization tuples?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: RecoverSigner constructs RLP-encoded authorization data, prepends SetCodeMagicPrefix (0x05), hashes with Keccak256, validates signature via TransactionSignatureIsValid, then recovers public key via crypto.Ecrecover.
identified_risks: TransactionSignatureIsValid checks: r != 0, s != 0, r < N, s < N, s <= N/2, v ∈ {0,1}
Signature recovery uses standard secp256k1 ecrecover

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Conforms to EIP-7702 specification for authorization signing
edge_cases_analyzed: Public key validation: Checked for length and format

audit_items.auditor_notes: EIP-7702 signature verification correctly implemented with proper ECDSA validation.

audit_items.title: Verify EIP-7702 Authorizer Authentication: Can an attacker forge authorization to impersonate the actor-eip7702-authorizer?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Authorization requires valid ECDSA signature over the authorization data. Without the private key, forging a signature is computationally infeasible under ECDSA security assumptions.

audit_items.auditor_notes: Authorization forgery is prevented by ECDSA signature requirement.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is the ECDSA signature s-value validated to be in the lower half of secp256k1 curve order?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: TransactionSignatureIsValid at line 293 checks: `if !allowPreEip2s && s.Gt(secp256k1halfN) { return false }`. For EIP-7702, allowPreEip2s=false is passed, enforcing s <= N/2.

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Conforms to EIP-2 (Homestead) signature malleability fix

audit_items.auditor_notes: S-value bound check correctly implemented in TransactionSignatureIsValid.

audit_items.title: Does signature malleability in EIP-7702 Authorization allow recovery to an unintended address?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 84: `if !crypto.TransactionSignatureIsValid(sig[64], &r, &s, false /* allowPreEip2s */) { return nil, errors.New("invalid signature") }`. The false parameter enforces EIP-2 s-value check, preventing malleability.

phase3_findings.formal_property: Malleable signatures (s > N/2) are rejected before recovery

audit_items.auditor_notes: Signature malleability prevented by enforcing s <= N/2 before ecrecover.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does the EIP-7702 authorization validation correctly reject ecrecover results returning address(0)?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Lines 88-92 check: `if len(pubKey) == 0 || pubKey[0] != 4 { return nil, errors.New("invalid public key") }`. Ecrecover errors are checked at line 86-87. The derived address from a valid pubkey will not be zero if pubkey is valid.
identified_risks: Empty pubkey: Rejected
Invalid pubkey format: Rejected
Ecrecover error: Returns error

edge_cases_analyzed: Invalid signature components: ecrecover returns error

audit_items.auditor_notes: Invalid signature recovery (including address(0) case) properly rejected.

audit_items.title: Is the transaction sender validation robust against address(0) authorization attacks at the P2P boundary?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: At lines 648-651, if RecoverSigner returns error, the authorization is skipped (continue). This prevents address(0) from being used as authority.

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Invalid authorizations are skipped per EIP-7702

audit_items.auditor_notes: P2P layer protected by authorization validation in verifyAuthorities.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the EIP-7702 Authorization chain_id field validated against the current chain ID?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Lines 640-644: `if !auth.ChainID.IsZero() && chainID != auth.ChainID.String() { log.Debug(...); continue }`. Chain ID validation allows exact match OR chain_id=0 (wildcard).
identified_risks: chain_id=0 allows cross-chain replay (per EIP-7702 specification)
Non-zero chain_id must match exactly

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Conforms to EIP-7702 - chain_id=0 is wildcard

remaining_concerns: chain_id=0 wildcard is intentional per spec but users should be aware

audit_items.auditor_notes: Chain ID validation correctly implemented per EIP-7702. Wildcard (0) behavior is by design.

audit_items.title: Does the EIP-7702 Authorizer actor enforce chain_id binding before signing delegation authorizations?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: The authorization data includes ChainID in the RLP encoding at lines 49-52. This is included in the hash that is signed.

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: ChainID is part of signed message

audit_items.auditor_notes: Chain ID is included in the signed authorization data, preventing post-signature modification.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is EIP-7702 Authorization nonce validation correctly enforced?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Lines 685-695: Nonce is fetched from state, compared with auth.Nonce. Must match exactly. Authorization skipped if mismatch.

audit_items.auditor_notes: Nonce validation correctly enforced before authorization processing.

audit_items.title: Can an attacker replay an EIP-7702 Authorization after the authorizer's nonce has incremented?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: After successful authorization, nonce is incremented at line 718-721. Subsequent replay attempts with same auth.Nonce will fail the nonce check.

audit_items.auditor_notes: Replay protection confirmed through nonce increment after successful authorization.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-006: Is the authorizer's nonce incremented after successful EIP-7702 authorization processing?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 718-721: `if err := st.state.SetNonce(authority, authorityNonce+1); err != nil { return nil, ... }`. Nonce increment happens after successful code delegation.

audit_items.auditor_notes: Nonce increment correctly implemented after successful authorization.

audit_items.title: Verify EIP-7702 Authorization Replay Protection: Can the same authorization be accepted twice?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Second submission of same authorization will fail nonce check since nonce was incremented after first successful processing.

audit_items.auditor_notes: Same authorization cannot be accepted twice due to nonce increment.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-001: Is the resolution of multiple EIP-7702 Authorizations targeting the same authorizer deterministic?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Authorizations are processed in order via `for i, auth := range auths`. Each successful auth increments nonce, so subsequent auths for same authority with same nonce will fail.
identified_risks: Last valid authorization for an authority takes effect (within single tx)
Deterministic due to sequential processing

audit_items.auditor_notes: Multiple authorizations for same authority are processed deterministically in order.

audit_items.title: Does the transaction sender have the ability to craft authorization sequences that produce implementation-specific behavior?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Processing is fully deterministic based on authorization order and state. No implementation-specific behavior paths identified.

phase3_findings.formal_property: ∀ impl1, impl2: result(impl1, auths) == result(impl2, auths)

audit_items.auditor_notes: No implementation-specific behavior identified in authorization processing.

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 124-126: `if l.Address == depositContractAddress && len(l.Topics) > 0 && l.Topics[0] == depositTopic`. Both address AND topic are validated.

audit_items.auditor_notes: Both address and topic validation correctly implemented.

audit_items.title: Verify Deposit Contract Address Integrity: Is DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS correctly defined and immutable?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: depositContractAddress is passed as parameter from chain config. It is defined in chain configuration and not modifiable at runtime.

phase2_findings.spec_conformance: Deposit contract address from chain config

audit_items.auditor_notes: Deposit contract address is sourced from chain configuration.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does parse_deposit_requests correctly filter logs by topic before processing?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Topic filtering at line 124: `len(l.Topics) > 0 && l.Topics[0] == depositTopic`. Logs with empty topics or wrong topic are skipped.

audit_items.auditor_notes: Topic filtering correctly implemented with empty topic array check.

audit_items.title: Verify Deposit Contract Log Integrity: Can a malicious transaction cause the deposit contract to emit logs that bypass topic filtering?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Topic filtering is applied regardless of how logs are emitted. Only logs with exact topic match are processed.

audit_items.auditor_notes: Log filtering is robust against malicious log emission.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does extract_deposit_data correctly reject deposit event data where length != 576 bytes?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: Line 63-64: `if len(data) != DepositLogLen { return InvalidDepositLogErr }`. DepositLogLen is 576 at line 33.

audit_items.auditor_notes: Deposit data length validation correctly implemented.

audit_items.title: Verify Deposit Contract Event Handling: Are malformed deposit events from the EL node properly validated at the trust boundary?

phase1_findings.code_analysis: validateDepositLog performs comprehensive validation: length check, offset validation, and field size validation. All checks must pass before data extraction.

phase3_findings.formal_property: All deposit log fields validated before processing

audit_items.auditor_notes: Deposit event validation is comprehensive and correct.
